name: vscode-mcp-server
description: Turn VS Code into an MCP server — file ops, symbols, diagnostics, tests, and persistent memory for AI coding assistants.

vscode-mcp-server.port.description: The port number for the MCP server

vscode-mcp-server.host.description: Host address for the MCP server

vscode-mcp-server.defaultEnabled.description: Whether the MCP server should be enabled by default on VS Code startup

markdownEnumDescriptions: A random secret is generated once and required on every call (recommended)
You pin the secret yourself in #vscode-mcp-server.auth.staticToken#
MCP OAuth 2.1 with dynamic client registration — what remote clients like Mammouth require
API key — stored in VS Code SecretStorage (OS keychain), auto-generated on first use. Clients send Authorization: Bearer <key>
No authentication (any local process or web page can run tools — not recommended)
vscode-mcp-server.auth.mode.description: How clients must authenticate to the MCP endpoint.

vscode-mcp-server.auth.staticToken.description: Token required when auth.mode is static-token. Pick a long random string (32+ characters).

vscode-mcp-server.auth.apiKey.description: API key required when auth.mode is api-key. If left empty, a key is auto-generated on first activation and stored securely in VS Code SecretStorage.

vscode-mcp-server.auth.allowedOrigins.description: Extra Origin values allowed besides the server's own (e.g. https://mammouth.ai when it calls through a tunnel). Browser requests from other sites stay blocked.

vscode-mcp-server.auth.allowNoOrigin.description: Accept requests that carry no Origin header (curl, SDK clients). Browsers always send Origin on cross-site posts, so this does not weaken the drive-by protection.

enumDescriptions: Every tool is listed, as before the twilight gate.
Only session_bootstrap_code is listed at first; its first call unlocks the full list and notifies the client.

Only session_bootstrap_code is ever listed. Every other tool stays callable by name or through session_bootstrap_code(action="call"). Keeps the schema cache small in clients that list tools once (Mammouth AI).
vscode-mcp-server.toolListing.description: Which tools the server advertises in tools/list. After a change, restart the server, then remove and re-add the connector in your MCP client.

vscode-mcp-server.twilightGate.description: Twilight gate: clients that call tools/list once cache every schema forever (Mammouth AI). With the gate on, tools/list returns ONLY session_bootstrap_code; the first session_bootstrap_code call unlocks the whole catalog for the server process. Server restart applies a change; the MCP client must also remove and re-add the connector so it lists again.

vscode-mcp-server.twilightStrict.description: Twilight strict mode (implies #vscode-mcp-server.twilightGate#): tools/list NEVER returns more than session_bootstrap_code, even after the gate is passed — connector pop-ups that re-list can never re-cache the other schemas. Every other tool stays callable by name (tools/call accepts it) but is never advertised; the agent guide remains their only catalog.

vscode-mcp-server.agentInstructions.description: Override the agent guide returned by get_agent_instructions_code (and copied by 'MCP Server: Copy Agent Instructions'). Leave empty to use the built-in guide: the complete tool catalog grouped by task with workflow rules, common recipes and approval behavior.

vscode-mcp-server.security.sandbox.mode.description: Filesystem confinement for authenticated tools. 'workspace': only folders open in this window plus allowPaths. 'home': the user profile directory. 'full': no restriction (dangerous with remote clients).

vscode-mcp-server.security.sandbox.allow.description: Extra absolute paths allowed when sandbox.mode is 'workspace' (e.g. D:\Mammouth\docs). Symlinks pointing outside are still refused.

markdownEnumDescriptions: Ask in VS Code before sensitive browser calls: JavaScript evaluation, file uploads, anything that reads or writes a local file, non-web URLs (recommended)
Also ask before every action that changes the page: navigation, clicks, typing, form filling
Never ask (only for a trusted, local client)
vscode-mcp-server.browser.confirm.description: When browser tools need your confirmation in VS Code.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.showActivity.description: Show the agent's activity in the page: a glowing frame and a label while it works, and a cursor that moves to each element before a click or a fill. Hidden from screenshots and page snapshots.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.activityLabel.description: Text of the label shown at the bottom of the page while the agent works.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.bringToFront.description: Bring the Chrome window to the front after the first page opens (Windows may only flash the taskbar button).

vscode-mcp-server.browser.headless.description: Run Chrome without a visible window.

markdownEnumDescriptions: A separate Chrome window with its own profile, kept between sessions (sign in once, cookies stay). Location: #vscode-mcp-server.browser.userDataDir# or ~/.cache/chrome-devtools-mcp

Your own Chrome, already open, with your tabs, cookies and logins. Needs Chrome 144+ and remote debugging switched on once at chrome://inspect/#remote-debugging. A remote client then acts with your logged-in sessions: keep the API key secret
A throwaway profile wiped when the browser closes
vscode-mcp-server.browser.profile.description: Which Chrome profile the browser tools use.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.userDataDir.description: Folder of the dedicated Chrome profile (profile = dedicated). Empty: ~/.cache/chrome-devtools-mcp/chrome-profile. Must not be the profile your everyday Chrome has open.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.hideAutomation.description: Hide Chrome's "controlled by automated test software" bar (Chrome does not allow changing its text). Applies when the extension launches Chrome.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.browserUrl.description: Connect to an already running Chrome started with --remote-debugging-port (e.g. http://127.0.0.1:9222) instead of launching one.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.executablePath.description: Path to the Chrome executable. Empty: the installed stable Chrome.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.allowFileUrls.description: Allow the browser to open file:// URLs (lets a remote client read local files through the browser).

vscode-mcp-server.browser.idleTimeoutMin.description: Close the browser after this many minutes without a browser call. 0 keeps it open.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.package.description: npm package started with npx when browser.command is empty.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.command.description: Executable that starts Chrome DevTools MCP (e.g. a global chrome-devtools-mcp install). Empty: npx -y <browser.package>.

vscode-mcp-server.browser.extraArgs.description: Extra command-line flags for Chrome DevTools MCP (e.g. --viewport=1280x720).

file.description: Enable file operations tools (read, write, list files)

edit.description: Enable file editing tools (create, edit, delete files)

symbol.description: Enable code symbol and structure analysis tools

memory.description: Enable persistent memory tools (load, save, search, clear)

test.description: Enable testing tools (run tests, coverage, format, lint, diff)

git.description: Enable git workflow tools (commit, branch, blame, conflicts, stash)

documentation.description: Enable documentation tools (dependencies, history, docstrings, project context, TODOs)

database.description: Enable developer productivity tools (SQL queries, API tests, env vars, ports, dev server)

productivity.description: Enable AI productivity tools (dead code finder, workspace snapshots, regex tester, encoding converter)

security.description: Enable security tools (secret scanning, risky-construct scan, dependency audit)

performance.description: Enable performance tools (bundle analysis, server report, command profiling)

refactoring.description: Enable refactoring tools (rename symbol, extract function, duplicate finder, suggestions)

frontend.description: Enable frontend tools (accessibility audit, CSS analysis, element inspection, unused CSS)

workflow.description: Enable workflow tools (task runner, build detection, snippets, shell aliases)

advanced.description: Enable advanced tools (server info with local usage stats, extension inventory)

skills.description: Enable agent-skill management tools (list, validate, package, scaffold SKILL.md-based skills)

ocr.description: Enable PDF OCR tools (scanned-page detection and text extraction via poppler-utils and tesseract)

browser.description: Enable browser tools: a Chrome browser driven through Chrome DevTools MCP (started on first use, needs Node.js and Chrome)

vscode-mcp-server.enabledTools.description: Configure which MCP tools are enabled
